## Analysis Results

After examining all small SUV categories with their hybrid/plug-in variants, here's the situation:

### Plug-in Hybrid Small SUVs with IIHS Top Safety Picks for 2023:

| Vehicle | Rating | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| **Toyota RAV4 Prime** | Top Safety Pick | Small SUV, Plug-in Hybrid |
| Lexus NX Plug-in Hybrid | Top Safety Pick+ | **Small Luxury SUV** category |
| Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV | Top Safety Pick | **EXCLUDED** (you don't want Mitsubishi) |

1. **No non-Mitsubishi small SUV plug-in hybrid earned Top Safety Pick+** - The only vehicle outside your Mitsubishi exclusions that achieved the highest safety rating was the Lexus NX Plug-in Hybrid, but it falls under the "Small Luxury SUV" category rather than the standard "Small SUV" category.

   - ✅ **Small SUV** (not luxury category)

   - The IIHS had significantly tougher testing criteria in 2023
   - Only one non-Mitsubishi plug-in hybrid small SUV qualified: the RAV4 Prime
   - Even the Lexus NX Plug-in Hybrid qualified only in the larger luxury category

This vehicle provides you with:
- The highest safety rating achievable in your target category
- A true plug-in hybrid powertrain
- No Mitsubishi branding
- All IIHS-required advanced safety features (Superior front crash prevention, Good headlight ratings, Advanced pedestrian detection)

Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS # **Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS** New, tougher crash tests mean there are fewer Top Safety Picks than last year By Keith Barry Senior Autos Reporter Updated by Jeff S. Bartlett Updated December 20, 2023 Photo: IIHS The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety’s annual list of cars with top scores in crash tests and other safety evaluations is growing, with further additions since the original February 2023 release. Even still, the list is shorter than in prior years because the tests are getting tougher. And that means the cars that meet the standards for being a Top Safety Pick are safer than ever. A tougher side impact crash test, a more comprehensive evaluation of automatic emergency braking (AEB), and new headlight requirements have raised the bar this year, making it tougher for vehicles to achieve the coveted TSP designations. These changes are designed to replicate real-world situations where crashes can take place. More On car Safety Car Safety and Fuel Efficiency Improvements Aren't Driving Up the Cost of Cars Small Cars Exceed Expectations in Tougher IIHS Side Impact Testing Ford’s BlueCruise Ousts GM’s Super Cruise As CR’s Top-Rated Active Driving Assistance System Most Vehicles Need Better Nighttime Automatic Emergency Braking In order to earn the highest ranking of Top Safety Pick+, vehicles had to earn an Acceptable or Good score on a new side crash test that’s designed to replicate a higher-speed impact with a larger vehicle, such as a modern SUV or pickup. In addition, the vehicles must have automatic emergency braking (AEB) systems that could prevent a collision with a pedestrian at nighttime, and they must come with good-performing headlights that illuminate the road ahead on curves and straightaways, regardless of vehicle trim levels. Studies have shown that most AEB systems don’t work as well in the dark, even though the majority of pedestrian crash fatalities take place at night. This requirement is meant to drive improvements to address this growing safety concern. # **Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS** “While different vehicles missed out for different reasons, the new headlight requirement is an issue for quite a few models,” says Joe Young, a spokesperson for the IIHS. Now that standard good or acceptable headlights are required for both awards, quite a few vehicles that qualified for last year’s award have fallen off the list this year, in part because they are still offered with Poor- or Marginal-rated headlights on base trims. For example, the Ford Mustang Mach-E would otherwise qualify for a 2023 Top Safety Pick+ if not for Marginal-rated headlights that come on several less expensive trims. Toyota, Lexus, Honda, Acura, and Mazda stand out for the most accolades from the IIHS, a safety-focused organization funded by the auto insurance industry. A Rivian R1T after a moderate-overlap front crash test. It's an IIHS Top Safety Pick+ winner. Photo: IIHS Photo: IIHS As the IIHS tests vehicles throughout the year, more cars have been added to the list. According to Young, some models—including the Chrysler Pacifica and Cadillac CT6—haven’t yet completed all the tests necessary for a 2023 award. Either one or both of these vehicles could end up on the list later this year. “Depending on how it performs, it may still earn an award,” he says. More models will likely earn Top Safety Pick+ status as the IIHS continues to raise the bar for the award, says Jennifer Stockburger, director of operations at CR’s auto test center. “Car manufacturers respond to tougher tests by designing new vehicles that can pass those tests,” she says. Manufacturers have been aware of the new side crash test since 2018, and models designed specifically with that test in mind are only now hitting the market. Consumer Reports uses IIHS ratings as part of the safety component for our Overall Score, which also factors in road-test performance, reliability, and owner satisfaction. # **Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS** Young says that shoppers who are interested in a vehicle that doesn’t appear on the list should first check out where it underperforms. In the case of headlights, buyers may be able to choose a higher trim level or optional feature that has better performance. If a vehicle comes up short in multiple categories, he says, “consider other options within the same class that provide a higher level of crashworthiness and crash avoidance performance.” A Volkswagen ID.4 EV after an IIHS crash test. It is a Top Safety Pick+ winner. Photo: IIHS Photo: IIHS Below, you will find the full list of new cars, SUVs, and trucks that earned the IIHS Top Safety Pick or Top Safety Pick+ award for the 2023 model year. Now that standard good or acceptable headlights are required for both awards, quite a few vehicles that qualified for last year’s award have fallen off the list this year, in part because they are still offered with Poor- or Marginal-rated headlights on base trims. For example, the Ford Mustang Mach-E would otherwise qualify for a 2023 Top Safety Pick+ if not for Marginal-rated headlights that come on several less expensive trims.
Toyota, Lexus, Honda, Acura, and Mazda stand out for the most accolades from the IIHS, a safety-focused organization funded by the auto insurance industry.

Manufacturers have been aware of the new side crash test since 2018, and models designed specifically with that test in mind are only now hitting the market.

# What Makes the Toyota Rav4 a Top Safety Pick?
Look at your various options for a new vehicle, and you will likely be concerned about the safety ratings. Toyota has a reputation of manufacturing incredibly safe and reliable models, including the Rav4. The 2016 Toyota Rav4 is a small SUV that received the top possible safety rating from the IIHS, that of a Top Safety Pick+.

# What Makes the Toyota Rav4 a Top Safety Pick?
### Toyota Rav4 Safety Ratings
Each year, the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, abbreviated IIHS, puts all new models through rigorous testing to determine their safety in various collisions. The 2016 Rav4 received the organization’s top rating of “Good” for small and moderate overlap front, side crashworthiness, and roof strength, as well as head restraints and seats. These ratings helped it reach the status of a Top Safety Pick. To become a Top Safety Pick+, the Rav4 also earned a “Superior” rating for the available front crash prevention system.

# What Makes the Toyota Rav4 a Top Safety Pick?
### Toyota Rav4 Standard Safety Features
To help it achieve these truly impressive safety ratings and the status of a Top Safety Pick, the Rav4 comes with a long list of standard safety features. These include front side torso airbags mounted to the seats and head curtain airbags in the front and rear, as well as a rollover sensor that will deploy these side curtain airbags if a rollover is about to occur. There is also a driver knee airbag and seat cushion airbag. Other standard safety on the Rav4 includes daytime running lights, antilock brakes, and electronic stability control.
Start driving the extremely safe 2016 Toyota Rav4 around Manassas, Virginia, after a test drive at Miller Toyota.

Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS # **Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS** New, tougher crash tests mean there are fewer Top Safety Picks than last year By Keith Barry Senior Autos Reporter Updated by Jeff S. Bartlett Updated December 20, 2023 Photo: IIHS The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety’s annual list of cars with top scores in crash tests and other safety evaluations is growing, with further additions since the original February 2023 release. Even still, the list is shorter than in prior years because the tests are getting tougher. And that means the cars that meet the standards for being a Top Safety Pick are safer than ever. A tougher side impact crash test, a more comprehensive evaluation of automatic emergency braking (AEB), and new headlight requirements have raised the bar this year, making it tougher for vehicles to achieve the coveted TSP designations. These changes are designed to replicate real-world situations where crashes can take place. More On car Safety Car Safety and Fuel Efficiency Improvements Aren't Driving Up the Cost of Cars Small Cars Exceed Expectations in Tougher IIHS Side Impact Testing Ford’s BlueCruise Ousts GM’s Super Cruise As CR’s Top-Rated Active Driving Assistance System Most Vehicles Need Better Nighttime Automatic Emergency Braking In order to earn the highest ranking of Top Safety Pick+, vehicles had to earn an Acceptable or Good score on a new side crash test that’s designed to replicate a higher-speed impact with a larger vehicle, such as a modern SUV or pickup. In addition, the vehicles must have automatic emergency braking (AEB) systems that could prevent a collision with a pedestrian at nighttime, and they must come with good-performing headlights that illuminate the road ahead on curves and straightaways, regardless of vehicle trim levels. Studies have shown that most AEB systems don’t work as well in the dark, even though the majority of pedestrian crash fatalities take place at night. This requirement is meant to drive improvements to address this growing safety concern. # **Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS** “While different vehicles missed out for different reasons, the new headlight requirement is an issue for quite a few models,” says Joe Young, a spokesperson for the IIHS. Now that standard good or acceptable headlights are required for both awards, quite a few vehicles that qualified for last year’s award have fallen off the list this year, in part because they are still offered with Poor- or Marginal-rated headlights on base trims. For example, the Ford Mustang Mach-E would otherwise qualify for a 2023 Top Safety Pick+ if not for Marginal-rated headlights that come on several less expensive trims. Toyota, Lexus, Honda, Acura, and Mazda stand out for the most accolades from the IIHS, a safety-focused organization funded by the auto insurance industry. A Rivian R1T after a moderate-overlap front crash test. It's an IIHS Top Safety Pick+ winner. Photo: IIHS Photo: IIHS As the IIHS tests vehicles throughout the year, more cars have been added to the list. According to Young, some models—including the Chrysler Pacifica and Cadillac CT6—haven’t yet completed all the tests necessary for a 2023 award. Either one or both of these vehicles could end up on the list later this year. “Depending on how it performs, it may still earn an award,” he says. More models will likely earn Top Safety Pick+ status as the IIHS continues to raise the bar for the award, says Jennifer Stockburger, director of operations at CR’s auto test center. “Car manufacturers respond to tougher tests by designing new vehicles that can pass those tests,” she says. Manufacturers have been aware of the new side crash test since 2018, and models designed specifically with that test in mind are only now hitting the market. Consumer Reports uses IIHS ratings as part of the safety component for our Overall Score, which also factors in road-test performance, reliability, and owner satisfaction. # **Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS** Young says that shoppers who are interested in a vehicle that doesn’t appear on the list should first check out where it underperforms. In the case of headlights, buyers may be able to choose a higher trim level or optional feature that has better performance. If a vehicle comes up short in multiple categories, he says, “consider other options within the same class that provide a higher level of crashworthiness and crash avoidance performance.” A Volkswagen ID.4 EV after an IIHS crash test. It is a Top Safety Pick+ winner. # 2 Standard Hybrid Models Made the IIHS 2023 Top Safety Pick List
## The IIHS 2023 Top Safety Pick List
The Top Safety Pick designation from the IIHS is a much sought-after distinction for consumers who value vehicle safety, according to U.S. News. Only vehicles that perform well in a series of crash tests earn the award, including front, side, rear impact, and rollover tests. Many consumers use the IIHS Top Safety Pick rating to help them make informed purchasing decisions. Vehicles earning this award have demonstrated by passing all rigorous safety tests, so they are most likely to provide strong protection in the event of a crash.
The Top Safety Pick rating also factors the availability of specific safety features like automatic emergency braking and forward collision warning, which can assist vehicles in accident avoidance. Other important considerations are fuel efficiency, overall reliability, and price.
There are two levels of IIHS awards: the Top Safety Pick and Top Safety Pick+.
To earn the IIHS Top Safety Pick award, the vehicle must have a rating of Good in all six crash tests with an Advanced or Superior rating for its available front crash prevention technology. The vehicle’s headlights must earn either a Good or Acceptable rating also.
To earn the IIHS Top Safety Pick+ award, the vehicle must meet all the criteria for the Top Safety Pick award with a Superior rating for front crash prevention technology and a Good headlight rating.

# 2 Standard Hybrid Models Made the IIHS 2023 Top Safety Pick List
## The 2023 Toyota Sienna
2023 Toyota Sienna | Toyota Motor Sales, U.S.A., Inc.
The 2023 Toyota Sienna won a Top Safety Pick+ award in the minivan category.
Yes, there are still a few minivans around. The Sienna has rugged exterior looks, excellent gas mileage thanks to its hybrid powertrain, and a refined driving experience, according to Car and Driver.
While the Sienna might be trying to pass itself off as an SUV, it’s hard to take issue with its refined ride and quiet cabin. Just be aware that the engine has a buzzy sound under heavy throttle. The Sienna is still a minivan with all the benefits that come with it. The interior is well-appointed and roomy, although you can’t remove the second row of seating.
In its fourth generation, the Sienna is only available as a hybrid with front and all-wheel drive. Its fuel economy is impressive, with a 36 mpg combined rating.

# 2 Standard Hybrid Models Made the IIHS 2023 Top Safety Pick List
## The 2023 Toyota Venza
The 2023 Toyota Venza earned a Top Safety Pick award in the small SUV segment. An Average rating on the vehicle’s headlights kept it from earning the Top Safety Pick+ award.
Car and Driver calls the Venza a RAV4 in a designer suit. They like its stylish exterior lines and its trick electrochromic panoramic roof. The two-row SUV is only available as a hybrid with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine and three electric motors, similar to the RAV4 Hybrid’s powertrain setup. It has all-wheel drive standard. The Venza’s fuel efficiency dominates the ratings of rivals such as the Honda Passport and Nissan Murano, both powered by V6 engines.
The 2023 Venza’s interior also beats the competition with better features, like the sunroof that changes from opaque to transparent with the touch of a button. Still, its sharp exterior styling tries to make up for the fact it only has a modest cargo area and tight passenger space.

Senior Autos Reporter
Updated by Jeff S. Bartlett
Updated December 20, 2023
Photo: IIHS
The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety’s annual list of cars with top scores in crash tests and other safety evaluations is growing, with further additions since the original February 2023 release. Even still, the list is shorter than in prior years because the tests are getting tougher. And that means the cars that meet the standards for being a Top Safety Pick are safer than ever.
A tougher side impact crash test, a more comprehensive evaluation of automatic emergency braking (AEB), and new headlight requirements have raised the bar this year, making it tougher for vehicles to achieve the coveted TSP designations. These changes are designed to replicate real-world situations where crashes can take place.

In order to earn the highest ranking of Top Safety Pick+, vehicles had to earn an Acceptable or Good score on a new side crash test that’s designed to replicate a higher-speed impact with a larger vehicle, such as a modern SUV or pickup. In addition, the vehicles must have automatic emergency braking (AEB) systems that could prevent a collision with a pedestrian at nighttime, and they must come with good-performing headlights that illuminate the road ahead on curves and straightaways, regardless of vehicle trim levels. Studies have shown that most AEB systems don’t work as well in the dark, even though the majority of pedestrian crash fatalities take place at night. This requirement is meant to drive improvements to address this growing safety concern.

# **Safest New Cars of 2023, According to the IIHS**
“While different vehicles missed out for different reasons, the new headlight requirement is an issue for quite a few models,” says Joe Young, a spokesperson for the IIHS. Now that standard good or acceptable headlights are required for both awards, quite a few vehicles that qualified for last year’s award have fallen off the list this year, in part because they are still offered with Poor- or Marginal-rated headlights on base trims. For example, the Ford Mustang Mach-E would otherwise qualify for a 2023 Top Safety Pick+ if not for Marginal-rated headlights that come on several less expensive trims.
Toyota, Lexus, Honda, Acura, and Mazda stand out for the most accolades from the IIHS, a safety-focused organization funded by the auto insurance industry.
A Rivian R1T after a moderate-overlap front crash test. It's an IIHS Top Safety Pick+ winner.
Photo: IIHS Photo: IIHS
As the IIHS tests vehicles throughout the year, more cars have been added to the list. According to Young, some models—including the Chrysler Pacifica and Cadillac CT6—haven’t yet completed all the tests necessary for a 2023 award. Either one or both of these vehicles could end up on the list later this year. “Depending on how it performs, it may still earn an award,” he says.
More models will likely earn Top Safety Pick+ status as the IIHS continues to raise the bar for the award, says Jennifer Stockburger, director of operations at CR’s auto test center. “Car manufacturers respond to tougher tests by designing new vehicles that can pass those tests,” she says. Manufacturers have been aware of the new side crash test since 2018, and models designed specifically with that test in mind are only now hitting the market.
Consumer Reports uses IIHS ratings as part of the safety component for our Overall Score, which also factors in road-test performance, reliability, and owner satisfaction.
